personas.name: Zara Malik
personas.headline: How Zara catches ideas before they vanish
personas.summary: Zara records on phone in the rickshaw, tags on iPad at the studio, reviews on laptop.

day.title: Voice capture
day.text: In the rickshaw Zara hits voice capture on her phone — if she can say it before the idea vanishes, it is saved on-device.

day.title: Tag on iPad
day.text: Studio iPad tags the morning captures by project so they do not drown in a single undated inbox.

day.title: Laptop review
day.text: Laptop idea list at end of day; she promotes one seed and parks the rest without guilt.

day.title: Note detail
day.text: Note detail on the laptop expands the keeper into something she can pitch tomorrow.

day.title: Phone
day.text: Phone inbox feels lighter. Saying it was enough to keep it.

personas.quote: If I can say it, it is saved.

personas.name: Kevin Ortiz
personas.headline: How Kevin keeps product ideas from drowning in Slack
personas.summary: Kevin dumps ideas on phone, sorts on iPad, decisions on laptop.

day.title: Quick capture
day.text: Kevin dumps a product idea on his phone before standup — Slack is not his notebook, and he is done pretending it is.

day.title: iPad sort
day.text: iPad sort by project at lunch; tags beat scrolling a year of threads for “that one thought.”

day.title: Laptop decide
day.text: Laptop note detail becomes a decision log — ship, park, or ask — instead of eternal emoji reactions.

day.title: Settings
day.text: Settings confirm offline-friendly habits; the ideas stay his even when the VPN sulks.

day.title: Phone
day.text: Phone clears. Ideas live in IdeaCap, not in a channel he will never search.

personas.name: Hamid Siddiqui
personas.headline: How Hamid keeps story seeds offline
personas.summary: Hamid writes on phone in the garden, expands on iPad, manuscripts on laptop — no account wall.

day.title: Garden phone
day.text: Garden morning: Hamid writes a story seed on his phone — offline is the point, no account wall between him and the line.

day.title: iPad expand
day.text: iPad expand turns the seed into a scene without uploading anything to a stranger’s cloud.

day.title: Laptop draft
day.text: Laptop draft gathers the day’s seeds into something that might become a chapter.

day.title: Laptop list
day.text: Ideas list on the laptop stays local; he owns the folder the way he owns the notebooks.

day.title: Phone
day.text: Phone locks. Offline won. The seed is still there.

video.transcript: Hamid works fully offline across phone, iPad, laptop. Fictional.
